label: MG-3300 manufactured 17Q4 (18 units): failure_to_start x2, ground_fault x2, cooling_airflow_low x2, hard_fault x1
headline: The MG-3300 17Q4 'cohort' is an artifact of six repeat visits on two Kernwood assets — per-asset failure rate is at the fleet median and every failure mode also appears at other sites, so there is no warranty case here.
action: Close the MG-3300/17Q4 cohort as not a build defect, and instead hand the two adjacent combiner-box conductor faults (WO-2025-00671, WO-2026-00050) and the open cable-sag walkdown items to the Kernwood site lead as a local BOS inspection task.
reasoning: The 9 member work orders resolve to only 5 distinct assets (WO-2025-01009, WO-2025-00858 and WO-2025-00823 are all MGX33-1742D-0354; WO-2025-00671, WO-2025-01193 and WO-2025-01227 are all MGX33-1740D-0301), so per-asset incidence is 5/18 = 0.28, exactly the peer median rather than the 0.50 headline rate — H1's central prediction confirmed. The symptom mix is maximally diffuse (6 modes, none exceeding 2) with no shared component or failure signature: a capacitor (WO-2024-00079), a control board (WO-2025-00193), two BOS combiner-box conductor faults (WO-2025-00671, WO-2026-00050), a bird nest, a seized fan and blocked filters — not the tight, repeating power-path signature a 17Q4 build defect would produce, which also refutes H3. The matched controls show the identical failure modes on other quarters and other sites: the same bird-nest-in-plenum event at Sawgrass (WO-2026-00195), the same seized-fan cooling alarm at Sawgrass (WO-2025-00291), and loaded filters as routine PM findings at Kernwood and Birch Coulee (WO-2024-00379, WO-2024-00232) — the members look like ordinary O&M, not a cohort. H2's site confound is real (all 9 members are at Kernwood Basin, with cable-sag findings in Kernwood walkdowns WO-2025-00127 and WO-2025-00021) but it is not separately actionable here and points to the same conclusion: nothing attributable to manufacturing quarter.
contradicting: Two DC ground faults in adjacent combiner boxes (WO-2025-00671 at CB-B08-17, WO-2026-00050 at CB-B09-14) plus two Kernwood cable-sag inspections (WO-2025-00127, WO-2025-00021) do suggest a genuine but site-local, BOS-scoped wiring/workmanship issue at Kernwood that is worth local attention even though it is unrelated to the MG-3300/17Q4 build. Resolution coding is also unreliable in the members (WO-2025-00671 closed NO-FAULT-FOUND after a repair; WO-2026-00050 closed RESET after a connector replacement; WO-2025-01227 lists a DC bus capacitor while the narrative says AC contactor; WO-2025-00193 lists IGBT modules while the narrative says control board), so any future re-test of this cohort should use narrative-derived fields rather than coded ones.

population_detail.description: No manufacturing-attributable population identified; the 18-unit 17Q4 cohort shows per-asset incidence at the peer median once repeat visits are collapsed.
population_detail.basis: 5 distinct asset_ids across the 9 member WOs divided by 18 units in cohort = 0.28/unit, equal to the stated peer median of 0.28.

hypotheses.statement: There is no real MG-3300/17Q4 build defect: 9 work orders on 18 units (0.50/unit vs peer median 0.28) is within ordinary Poisson variation for a small cohort, inflated further by three repeat visits each on two assets.
predictions: Distinct-asset count is far below member count (~4-5 unique asset_ids for 9 WOs), so per-asset incidence is close to peer
A Poisson/exact test on 9 observed vs ~5 expected over the same exposure window returns a non-significant p (>0.05)
Other MG-3300 mfg quarters with similarly small unit counts show comparable or higher rate_per_unit swings across the 10 peer quarters
Symptom mix is maximally diffuse (6 distinct symptoms / 9 WOs) with no single mode exceeding 2, i.e. no dominant failure signature
discriminating_evidence: Recompute rate using distinct assets rather than WO count, and pool 17Q4 units at OTHER sites: if non-Kernwood 17Q4 units sit at peer rate, the cohort signal dissolves
If a single symptom (e.g. capacitor failure_to_start) concentrated in >=5 distinct 17Q4 assets across >=2 sites, this hypothesis fails

hypotheses.statement: The cohort is a site/installation artifact: every member WO is at Kernwood Basin, and the drivers are local combiner-box workmanship (chafed/pinched home runs) plus local airborne debris and wildlife loading the cooling path, none of which is attributable to manufacturing quarter.
predictions: 100% of the 9 member WOs carry site == 'Kernwood Basin'
Both ground_fault WOs resolve to conductor_or_connector in combiner boxes with adjacent IDs (CB-B08-17, CB-B09-14), and similar DC GF/chafe WOs exist at Kernwood on non-17Q4 and non-MG-3300 assets
Kernwood-wide cooling_airflow_low / air_filter / wildlife_intrusion WO rate exceeds the fleet rate regardless of model or mfg quarter
17Q4 units at other sites show no elevation in ground_fault or cooling symptoms
discriminating_evidence: Cross-tab mfg_quarter x site: if the elevated rate holds for MG-3300 units of ALL quarters at Kernwood, it is a site effect; if it holds for 17Q4 units across ALL sites, it is a build effect
Check whether combiner-box conductor damage WOs at Kernwood are string/BOS-scoped (shared across inverters) rather than inverter-scoped

hypotheses.statement: A genuine 17Q4 build issue exists but is narrow — DC-link/contactor power-path components (DC bus capacitor, AC contactor) aging out early — and the ground-fault, wildlife and filter WOs are unrelated noise swept into the cluster by the symptom-agnostic grouping.
predictions: Restricting to power-path symptoms (failure_to_start, hard_fault, overcurrent_trip) still yields a rate above peer quarters for 17Q4
DC bus capacitor / contactor parts_used consumption per 17Q4 unit exceeds that of adjacent quarters (17Q3, 18Q1) on the same model
Time-to-first power-path WO for 17Q4 assets is systematically shorter than for other quarters, clustering around a similar service age
Repeat power-path failures appear on distinct asset_ids, not just the two frequent-flyer units
discriminating_evidence: Parts-consumption counts for DC bus capacitor per unit, split by mfg_quarter and by site — a quarter-specific spike that survives site stratification supports this; a Kernwood-only spike refutes it
Age-at-failure alignment: defect predicts tight clustering of first power-path WO age, random wear predicts a broad spread

hypotheses.statement: The cluster is partly a logging/technician artifact: TECH-0166 authored the majority of member WOs and low-severity P3 events closed as RESET / NO-FAULT-FOUND / CLEANED are being written up as separate corrective work orders that other techs or sites would not raise.
predictions: TECH-0166 appears on ~5 of 9 member WOs, well above that tech's share of fleet WOs
A high share of member WOs carry resolution_code in {RESET, NO-FAULT-FOUND, CLEANED} with parts_used empty
Removing zero-parts, P3, non-recurrence WOs drops the cohort rate to or below peer median

Extraction inconsistencies are visible (e.g. WO-2025-00193 parts_used 'IGBT module x3' vs narrative 'replaced the control board'; WO-2026-00050 resolution RESET vs action part_replaced), indicating coding noise
discriminating_evidence: Compare per-tech WO-raising rate per asset-year across the fleet; if TECH-0166's rate is elevated everywhere, the cohort signal is an authoring artifact
Compare lost_mwh_reported per WO for member vs peer WOs — if member events are materially lower-impact, they are reporting granularity rather than added failures
